Court No. - 16
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 1808 of 2023
Applicant :- Ritesh Gupta
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Ramakar Shukla
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1.
Heard Sri Ramakar Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri R.K. Verma, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the records.

2. The instant application has been filed by the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in F.I.R. bearing Case Crime No.629 of 2023, under Sections 376, 504, 506 I.P.C., registered at Police Station Kotwali Nagar, District Sultanpur.

3. The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of an F.I.R. lodged on 08.07.2023 stating that the informant, who is major, had developed a love relation with the applicant and under an allurement of marrying her, the applicant repeatedly made physical relation with the informant since April, 2022, but ultimately he declined to marry her.
In the statement of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. she reiterated the FIR version and stated that she and the informant were in a loving relationship.
Ritesh Gupta vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: Ritesh Gupta vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the affidavit filed in support of the anticipatory bail-application, it has been contended that the applicant is innocent, he has no criminal history and he has falsely been implicated in the present case.
5. The learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but he could not dispute the aforesaid aspects of the matter.
He submits that the investigation is going on.
In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
Ritesh Gupta vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
